title: Instruction List: calling an off-delay and an on-delay timer
summary: Call a TOF timer with CAL to keep a light on after a push button is released, and a TON timer to ignore a sensor blip that is too short, then read each timer output after its call.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real push button bounces or how fast a real sensor answers.
objectives: Call a timer instance with CAL on every scan, passing its input and its preset, and read its output after the call.
Keep an output on for a fixed time after its input drops, with a TOF, and ignore an input that is on for less than a fixed time, with a TON.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/Delays.il two timers are declared, HoldTimer (TOF) and FilterTimer (TON), and the program loads Button into Light and Sensor into Confirmed. Make Light stay ON for {{t:300}} ms after Button is released, and make Confirmed turn ON only after Sensor has stayed ON for {{t:200}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which of the two timers keeps an output on after its input falls, which one waits before it turns its output on, and which instruction runs a timer in IL.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario presses Button at {{t:100}} ms and releases it at {{t:300}} ms. Sensor blips ON from {{t:100}} ms to {{t:140}} ms and is ON again from {{t:500}} ms to {{t:900}} ms. Predict Light and Confirmed at {{t:200}}, {{t:450}}, {{t:650}} and {{t:800}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@200|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:200}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=true,Delays.Confirmed=false@450|Light ON, Confirmed OFF}} at {{t:450}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=false@650|both OFF}} at {{t:650}} ms; {{v:Delays.Light=false,Delays.Confirmed=true@800|Confirmed ON, Light OFF}} at {{t:800}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program loads each input and stores it in the output, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON with the short blip at {{t:100}} ms. Change it so that Light stays ON until {{t:300}} ms after Button is released, and Confirmed turns ON only when Sensor has been ON for {{t:200}} ms without a break. Write the instructions yourself: the declarations are already there.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named Delays and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow Light and Confirmed in the trace: the short blip never turns Confirmed ON, Light is still ON at {{t:450}} ms although Button went OFF at {{t:300}} ms, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after Sensor came back at {{t:500}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Light falls about {{t:300}} ms after Button, and Confirmed rises about {{t:200}} ms after the second Sensor pulse.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Swap the two timers in your head: what would a TON on Button and a TOF on Sensor do with this scenario? Then imagine the line that loads the Q of HoldTimer moved above its CAL: when would Light fall?
stages.checkpoint: TON delays the start and TOF delays the end; each answers a different question about a signal. In IL both are called the same way, so the declaration decides which one you get. Read above its CAL, Light would show the Q of the previous scan and fall one scan late.

hints.text: TOF keeps its Q on for the preset time after IN falls, and TON raises Q only after IN has been on for the preset time. CAL runs a timer with its inputs; after it, load the timer's Q and store it.
CAL HoldTimer(IN := Button, PT := T#300ms), LD HoldTimer.Q, ST Light; CAL FilterTimer(IN := Sensor, PT := T#200ms), LD FilterTimer.Q, ST Confirmed.

faultCases: The starting program loads each input and stores it in the output, so Light is already OFF at {{t:450}} ms and Confirmed turns ON with the short blip at {{t:100}} ms.
